title: DeepSeekCoTHandler plan-before-proving prompt: name intermediate lemmas and proof structure before the Lean proof
intent: Make the lemma skeleton a required planning step of every proof attempt: before writing any Lean code, the prompt asks the DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B chat model to produce a proof plan naming key ideas, intermediate lemmas and proof structures, then to complete the Lean code for a goal fixed as `:= by sorry`.

children.name: sorrify-goal
children.statement: Rewrite the input theorem into a sorry-able skeleton: split on the `:= by` marker and append `:= by sorry`

children.name: plan-first-prompt
children.statement: Ask the model to 'provide a detailed proof plan ... The plan should highlight key ideas, intermediate lemmas, and proof structures' before producing the Lean code

children.name: extract-code
children.statement: Extract the last ```lean4 code block from the model's raw output and prepend the import header

children.name: splice-proof
children.statement: Replace the `sorry` in the original statement with the extracted proof to yield the final code

applicability.goal_shape: A Lean theorem statement (ending in `:= by` or `:= by sorry`) whose proof body is to be generated by the DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B chat model; the goal is always presented as a fixed statement with an open `sorry` body
applicability.use_when: the prover is the DeepSeek chat model (whose model card expects `sorry` in the goal), and you want the model to name its intermediate lemmas and proof structure before it writes the proof; the model's raw output is then parsed for a ```lean4 code block
applicability.avoid_when: the prover is a completion-only (non-chat) model — DeepSeekNonCoTHandler (line 386) omits both the `sorry` and the plan — or when you need the plan parsed, validated, or checked against the proof (the harness only extracts the final code block and never reads the plan); or when the statement already has a proof body you must preserve (the `:= by sorry` rewrite discards it)

claims.claim: The prompt instructs the model to plan before proving: 'Before producing the Lean 4 code to formally prove the given theorem, provide a detailed proof plan ... The plan should highlight key ideas, intermediate lemmas, and proof structures that will guide the construction of the final formal proof.'

Line 340 fixes the goal as a sorry-able skeleton — it splits the input on ':=' by' and appends ':=' by sorry' — and line 341 wraps the result in 'Complete the following Lean 4 code', so the statement is fixed and only the proof body is open.

The plan is a soft instruction, not a checked artifact: extrac_code (lines 323-337) keeps only the last ```lean4 code block and problem_check (lines 352-354) splices that block into the statement via replace_statement_in_proof; no code in the copied file parses or validates the plan text.

The same think-before-proving instruction recurs in the correction-round prompt: 'Before producing the Lean 4 code to formally prove the given theorem, provide a detailed analysis of the error message' (line 372).
The authors explain the sorrify step in a comment: the ':=' by sorry' rewrite exists to 'include sorry' per the model card at huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B (line 340).

metrics.how_counted: pipeline_steps = the four handler stages the proof passes through in src/utils.py (sorrify-goal at prover_inference line 340, plan-first-prompt at line 341, extract-code at extrac_code lines 323-337, splice-proof at problem_check lines 352-354 -> replace_statement_in_proof lines 210-223); prompt_lines = the single F-string at line 341; plan_checked_mechanically = no code in the file parses the plan text

consequences: The plan is a soft instruction: the harness never parses, validates or rewards the plan, and extrac_code (lines 323-337) keeps only the last ```lean4 code block, which problem_check (lines 352-354) splices into the statement via replace_statement_in_proof (lines 210-223). Fidelity between the named intermediate lemmas and the final proof is therefore left entirely to the model. The ':=' by sorry' rewrite discards any existing proof body and must be undone by replace_statement_in_proof, which refuses proofs that use apply?/exact? (lines 211-212) or that lack the 'theorem ... :=' marker (lines 220-222). The prompt is tied to the DeepSeek chat template (tokenizer.apply_chat_template), so it cannot be reused for completion-only models.
